title: Tiles are seemingly randomly reset in the editor
body: I have seen this from Godot 4.0 RC2 through RC6 on two Linux systems using the Vulkan backend. Something in the editor intermittently removes properties from my TileSets, including terrain peering bits and physics-layer data. It can happen while working or after restarting the editor. Usually every terrain bit except the center bit disappears, and the Terrain painting tool then shows only Connect Mode and Path Mode. If I save after this happens, Git shows that the properties were actually deleted from the resource files on disk. I attached a minimal reproduction project, although the problem does not occur reliably.

symptoms_visible: My TileSets intermittently lose terrain peering bits and physics-layer properties; usually only the center terrain bit remains.
When this happens, the Terrain painting tool shows only Connect Mode and Path Mode.
If I save in that state, Git shows the missing properties have been deleted from the resource files.
N0.label: N0 intermittent TileSet data loss reported

symptoms_visible: In my production project, all tiles changed to the middle-only terrain state at the moment Godot regained focus.
Because I had saved before the reset, closing and reopening Godot restored the earlier TileSet state.
N1.label: N1 focus-change trigger observed

symptoms_visible: In another affected project, clicking another window and then returning to Godot removes the painted terrain and collision data within minutes.
Ordinary tile information such as animation remains, while the output fills with a very large number of errors.
N2.label: N2 reproducible affected project supplied

symptoms_visible: With the Dialogue Manager plugin present, adding a terrain, saving, and switching focus can remove the terrain markup or crash the editor.
With the plugin disabled, the terrain remains after the same focus-switch steps.
The reset still occurs when the plugin's focus-change path performs its resource-filesystem scan even if the rest of that handler is disabled.
N3.label: N3 resource scan trigger isolated

symptoms_visible: The same collision and terrain data loss also occurs in projects with no plugins installed.
When recreating the lost terrain data, the output can repeatedly report invalid terrain peering bits and a missing TileSet.
A vanilla development build can still lose entire physics layers.
N4.label: N4 engine-level issue established

symptoms_visible: After updating to a build containing the editor fixes, the focus-switch reproduction no longer removes the terrain markup.
The TileSet terrain and physics data remain intact, and the issue has not recurred during normal editing.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after update and retest

question_patterns: Can you identify what you were doing at the exact moment the TileSet reset occurred?
Does switching away from the editor and returning make the reset happen?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I finally saw it happen in my production project. I moved focus away from Godot, and the moment my mouse re-entered the window and Godot regained focus, all the tiles reset to the middle-only state. They had correct terrain assignments seconds earlier.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Switching focus never affects it; the properties disappear only after I manually remove a terrain from the set.
It happened when I clicked back into Godot rather than when the mouse first crossed into its window.

question_patterns: If you close the editor without saving the reset state and reopen the project, what do you see?
Can the previously saved TileSet be recovered by restarting Godot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had saved just before it happened, so I closed Godot and restarted it. That brought the correct saved TileSet back because I had not saved the reset state.

question_patterns: Can you still reproduce this in the original sample project?
Do you have an updated minimal project where the reset occurs reliably?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I still cannot make it happen reliably in the sample project. It occurred again in my production project, but I do not yet have a deterministic minimal reproduction.

edges.comment: From c4-c5 on MarcusRiemer's system: the maintainer requested an up-to-date reproduction, and the original reporter described the first precisely observed focus-return event, the unreliable sample project, and recovery by restarting without saving.

question_patterns: Can another affected user provide a project where this happens consistently?
Please attach the affected project and identify the TileMap and TileSet to inspect.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached my affected project. The TileMap is Farm.tscn/TileMaps/Back and the TileSet is BackSpring.tscn. In this project I can paint the terrain, click a window on my other monitor, and then click back into Godot; the painted data resets.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The attached project retains all TileSet data after repeated focus changes, and I can reproduce the loss only after manually editing the resource file.
The same project reproduces after using Alt-Tab instead of clicking the other monitor.

question_patterns: Which kinds of tile data disappear, and which properties remain?
Does the reset affect ordinary tile properties as well as painted collision and terrain data?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: All the painted TileSet data I save is removed, including collision masks and terrain details. Normal tile information, including tile animation, still saves correctly.

question_patterns: What appears in the output when the reset occurs?
Does the editor log any repeating errors at the same time?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The TileSet editor slows down and the output starts filling with errors. In one occurrence Godot generated more than 200,000 of them, and the output took several minutes to load.

question_patterns: Which scene node and TileSet resource should I open in the attached project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Open Farm.tscn, select TileMaps/Back, and inspect the TileSet named BackSpring.tscn.

edges.comment: From c6-c9 on SqueakyThePig's affected system, folded into the simulated user side: a second user supplied a consistently affected production project, screenshots of the before/after terrain state and error flood, and exact resource locations. KoBeWi could reproduce with that project.

question_patterns: Do the projects where this reproduces have any editor plugins in common?
Can you compare the enabled plugins in the reproducible projects?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The reproducible projects both have Dialogue Manager installed. I made another sample with Dialogue Manager 2.14.0 where adding a terrain, saving, and Alt-Tabbing away and back removes the terrain markup or sometimes crashes the editor.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reproducible projects have no editor plugins or scripts in common, and the reset occurs before any plugin is loaded.

question_patterns: If you disable the shared plugin and repeat the same save and focus-switch sequence, what happens?
Can you compare the same reproduction steps with that plugin enabled and disabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the plugin enabled, the terrain markup disappears after the save and focus switch. After disabling the plugin, I can repeat those steps and the terrain stays in place.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The terrain resets identically with the plugin disabled in the same sample project.
It takes several focus changes with the plugin enabled, but I still cannot trigger it after disabling the plugin.

question_patterns: Can you narrow the focus-change path down to the specific editor operation that coincides with the reset?
If you disable parts of the plugin's focus handler, which operation still triggers the TileSet loss?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I narrowed it down to the plugin calling get_editor_interface().get_resource_filesystem().scan() on focus change. The TileSet resets when that call runs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing that call makes no difference; the reset still occurs before the focus handler runs.
The plugin also updates the text shown in its own dock after focus changes.

question_patterns: Does the reset still happen if the plugin's other focus-handler work is disabled?
Can you separate the filesystem operation from the plugin's configuration update code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I disabled the handler code that updates the plugin's own JSON configurations, but left the resource-filesystem call in place, and the TileSet reset still happened.

edges.comment: From c12-c18 on sgt's sample and the already reproducible project: sgt found the shared Dialogue Manager plugin and isolated the raw trigger to its focus-change call to EditorFileSystem.scan(). KoBeWi observed that disabling the plugin avoids the reproduction. The plugin author's alternative call is not treated as the Godot-side fix.

question_patterns: Does the same TileSet data loss occur in projects with no plugins installed or enabled?
Can anyone reproduce missing collision or terrain data in a vanilla project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I have no plugins installed or running, but physics values and terrains still disappear from my TileSet. Saving the TileSet separately or making it unique does not prevent it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every confirmed occurrence uses Dialogue Manager, and a clean project without plugins remains intact through repeated editing and focus changes.
It also happens without plugins, but only to collision data rather than both collision and terrain data.

question_patterns: What exact errors appear while recreating the missing terrain data?
Can you paste the repeated TileSet-related output lines?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: While trying to redo the terrains, the output is spammed with 'Condition !is_valid_terrain_peering_bit(p_peering_bit) is true' and 'Condition !tile_set is true. Returning: false'.

question_patterns: Can you check whether a recent vanilla development build still shows the problem?
Does this continue in an unmodified unstable build with no plugins?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It also happened to me in a vanilla development build with no mods. An entire physics layer was wiped from the TileSet.

edges.comment: From c21-c28 on HelpfulFerret, Lertos, Proggle, and MewPurPur's separate systems, folded into one affected-user side: vanilla projects and a later development build exhibited the same class of terrain or physics-data loss. This falsifies treating Dialogue Manager itself as the root cause; it was one reliable trigger for an engine-side problem.

solution.intent: Treat this as an engine editor-resource scanning bug rather than a TileSet authoring mistake or a Dialogue Manager-specific defect. Update to a Godot build containing the editor fixes, avoid saving a TileSet after the reset is visible, and verify the fix by repeating the focus-switch reproduction.
solution.concrete_example: Install a current Godot build containing the relevant editor fixes, open the affected project, add or edit terrain data, save, switch focus away and back, and confirm that terrain and physics properties remain. Until updated, close without saving and reopen or revert the resource if the middle-only reset appears.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied the raw trigger and errors: a focus-change path called EditorFileSystem.scan(), the reset persisted when unrelated plugin handler code was disabled, and logs reported missing TileSet references and invalid terrain peering bits. Combining this with the maintainer's reproduction that TileData pointed to a nonexistent TileSet supports the engine-side diagnosis. The linked fix changes were not described in detail in the thread, so their internal mechanism should not be invented.

edges.comment: Resolution from c30-c33: maintainers linked two editor changes as potential fixes. sgt repeated the earlier focus-switch reproduction and could no longer trigger the loss, and Proggle reported no recurrence since updating. These are affected-user confirmations after the changes, so they are represented terminal-side rather than as required pre-solution evidence. The later TileMapLayer report in c34-c40 was explicitly judged unrelated and is excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a Godot editor resource-scanning problem: the focus-triggered filesystem scan can leave TileData without a valid TileSet reference, after which terrain and physics properties are removed and may be serialized to disk.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: focus return triggers the reset, a reproducible project exhibits the loss and error flood, the scan call was isolated, and output reports missing TileSet and invalid terrain-peering data.

Must not blame the Dialogue Manager plugin as the underlying defect or present updating that plugin as the complete fix; it provided a reliable scan trigger, but vanilla projects without plugins were also affected.
Must not dismiss the loss as user error or merely a stale editor display, since the missing properties are written to disk if the corrupted state is saved.

Must recommend a Godot build containing the editor fix and ask the user to repeat the focus-switch reproduction before declaring resolution; until then, the user should avoid saving the reset state and recover from a prior save or version control.
Resolution requires an affected user to confirm that the reproduction no longer removes TileSet data after updating.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Godot users working with TileSets, terrain painting, physics layers, Git, plugins, and minimal reproduction projects; one contributor can isolate plugin code paths, while others mainly provide observations and logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-oriented but cautious about uncertain triggers; provides screenshots, projects, exact editor steps, raw errors, and corrections when an earlier observation was mistaken.
